items.title: A vertex mixed on an anticonnected set yields opposite adjacency on a nonedge
items.strategy: Work in the complement of the anticonnected set. A mixed outside vertex has both a neighbour and a nonneighbour inside the set, and a shortest complement-path between those two sides produces a first edge whose endpoints are nonadjacent in the graph but have opposite adjacency to the outside vertex.

items.title: Mixed anticonnected blocks lift pattern obstructions to the ambient graph
items.strategy: Form the auxiliary graph on the mixed blocks, with edges for complete cross-pairs. The local mixed-on-anticonnected lemma supplies, inside each block, a neighbour/nonneighbour witness pair for the outside vertex. A clique in the auxiliary graph then yields the source's star-subdivision obstruction, while an induced copy of the chosen pattern lifts block-by-block because every nonedge of the auxiliary graph is realized by directional sparsity and every edge is realized by completeness.

items.title: The auxiliary pattern then has a polynomial-size clique or stable set
items.strategy: Use the previous obstruction-lifting lemma to show that the auxiliary graph is either K_t-free or free of the finite family that already has the Erdős-Hajnal property. The existing complete-graph Erdős-Hajnal theorem and the family-definition version of the Erdős-Hajnal property then give a polynomial-size clique or stable set in the auxiliary graph.

items.title: A polynomial homogeneous set in the auxiliary pattern yields a $y^4$-restricted union
items.strategy: Take the union of the equal-size blocks indexed by the clique or stable set in the auxiliary graph. A stable set gives pairwise y^a-sparse blocks, so each vertex sees at most r^{-1}|S| neighbours in its own block and at most y^a|S| outside; a clique gives the dense analogue. The source's exponent choice a >= 6 is exactly what makes the final r^{-1}+y^a <= y^4 estimate close.

items.title: Star and special-vertex obstructions force wonderfulness
items.strategy: Follow the Huang-Ju-Zhou Lemma 2.1 route through the auxiliary graph of mixed blocks. The proof is scaffolded explicitly through the mixed-anticonnected witness lemma, the pattern-obstruction lifting lemma, and the restricted-union lemma so that the step-5 author can keep the source's first-alternative seam visible instead of flattening it into a one-line citation.

items.title: The $E$-graph and the Bird graph are wonderful
items.strategy: Instantiate the previous criterion twice. For the E-graph, use the explicit one-subdivision of K_{1,3} that contains E as an induced subgraph. For Bird, use the six-vertex witness graph H from the source, note that a two-vertex homogeneous set lets H collapse to a five-vertex quotient with the Erdős-Hajnal property, and then verify the source's two local edits that produce induced co-Bird witnesses inside the corresponding H^+ and H^- graphs.

title: Leaf Reducibility and Wonderful Families — Examples

items.title: The $E$-graph sits inside a one-subdivided star and deletes to the five-vertex path
items.strategy: Write the one-subdivision of K_{1,3} explicitly and identify a six-vertex induced subset isomorphic to E. The same vertex list shows that deleting the pendant leaf from E recovers P_5, which is the leaf-reducible side of the later route.

items.title: A six-vertex witness graph makes the Bird criterion explicit
items.strategy: Write down the source's six-vertex graph H, isolate its homogeneous pair, and check the five-vertex quotient that already has the Erdős-Hajnal property. Then verify directly the two induced co-Bird configurations that the source reads off from the corresponding H^+ and H^- graphs.
